season_compatibility: Workable only if T. Aman is harvested and the field drained early: high-yielding rabi crops need establishing by early December, but in the Polder 30/43/PSTU trials aman was harvested 12 Nov-10 Dec and land often stays flooded or saturated until December. Aman duration decides the gap: BRRI dhan62 100 d, dhan33 118 d, dhan72 125 d, dhan52 140 d. Hybrid maize Pacific 984 has a 135-day field duration. In Dacope (Khulna) 15 Dec sowing gave the best maize yield and sowing just after T. Aman harvest is advised with zero tillage.
water_implications: Polder 30 rabi crops relied on residual soil moisture and rainfall only (no irrigation after 2013 because canal water became unsuitable). Maize still gave 5.7-6.7 t/ha rainfed in the 2013-14 and 2015-16 dry seasons but was hit by both drought and excess rain in different years; Pacific 984 is listed as drought tolerant.
soil_nutrient_implications: Maize is a cereal following a cereal, with no legume credit. FAO ECOCROP: high maize yields make a heavy drain on soil nutrients and maize has a high nitrogen requirement, so N (and K) replacement must be planned.
salinity_implications: Polder 30 topsoil salinity 2-16 dS/m; soil salinity is lowest Jul-Dec (monsoon and tidal water leach salts), intermediate Jan-Mar, and highest Apr-May (Polder 30 study). Rabi crops therefore meet rising salinity the later they are sown. ECOCROP places maize tolerance at low salinity (<4 dS/m optimal, 4-10 dS/m absolute); in a Botiaghata trial salt-tolerant hybrid lines reached up to 11.37 t/ha.
waterlogging_implications: Maize is waterlogging-sensitive; T. Aman soils commonly stay saturated for about 15-45 days after harvest depending on topography, which delays sowing. Systematic sluice-gate drainage (terminal drainage by mid-November) is the stated prerequisite. About 500 mm of cyclone rain in May 2013 damaged all Polder 30 rabi crops.
system_yield_evidence: Khulna (Polder 30): Fallow-Rice-Maize rice-equivalent yield 10.0 t/ha/yr vs Fallow-Rice-Rice 8.0 and farmers' fallow-rice-sesame 4-5; aman-rabi range 6.6-10.0 with maize highest and among the most stable.
region: Polder 30, Batiaghata, Khulna (system yield); Dacope, Khulna (sowing date); Botiaghata (salt-tolerant lines)
source: Mondal et al. 2020 JISCAR 38(2); Akther et al. 2024 JISCAR 42(1); JISCAR wheat waterlogging paper; FAO ECOCROP; SAU journal Botiaghata maize lines
notes: Sowing date of the Polder 30 maize plots is not stated in the source. Pest/disease break: no source found.

season_compatibility: Sunflower is sown by dibbling directly into wet soil right after T. Aman harvest (mid-November) in SRDI trials at Batiaghata, which avoids tillage delay. Hysun 33 has a 110-day field duration. Same early-drainage prerequisite as other rabi crops (establish by early December).
water_implications: Grown on residual moisture and rainfall in Polder 30; Hysun 33 is listed as drought tolerant. A BARI scientist states sunflower can be cultivated with two irrigations in the south of Bangladesh. FAO: deep root system (2-3 m) explores deep soil water.
soil_nutrient_implications: FAO general guidance (not site-tested): about 50-100 kg N, 20-45 kg P and 60-125 kg K per ha; crop is particularly sensitive to boron deficiency.
pest_disease_break: Sunflower is a susceptible host of Sclerotinia sclerotiorum (white mold); sclerotia survive 3-5 years in soil and cereals/grasses are non-hosts. Field flooding at warm temperatures destroys sclerotia, so a flooded T. Aman crop before sunflower is expected to help (inference from general evidence; not measured in Polder 30).
salinity_implications: Polder 30 topsoil salinity 2-16 dS/m; soil salinity is lowest Jul-Dec (monsoon and tidal water leach salts), intermediate Jan-Mar, and highest Apr-May (Polder 30 study). Rabi crops therefore meet rising salinity the later they are sown. FAO: sunflower emergence is 80-100% at ECe 0.7 dS/m, about 75% at 4.5, 30-60% at 9.5; later growth stages are moderately tolerant. Hysun-33 outperformed Local and BARI Sunflower-2 on saline land in Batiaghata and Chalna trials.
waterlogging_implications: Polder 30 rainfed sunflower (yield 1.0-2.9 t/ha) suffered drought or waterlogging depending on the year; a waterlogging tolerance value for sunflower was not found.
system_yield_evidence: Khulna (Polder 30): Fallow-Rice-Sunflower rice-equivalent yield 8.5 t/ha/yr; aman-rabi with sunflower more stable across years than mungbean or sesame.
region: Polder 30, Batiaghata, Khulna; SRDI Salinity Management & Research Center, Batiaghata
source: Mondal et al. 2020 JISCAR 38(2); Financial Express (SRDI Batiaghata trial); FAO Land & Water sunflower page; UNB (BARI statement); PNW Handbook; NDSU
notes: Waterlogging tolerance value: no source found. Sclerotinia effect of T. Aman flooding is an inference.

season_compatibility: Traditional Polder 30 pattern (aman-mungbean). Mungbean was sown 8 Feb-16 Mar on residual moisture and harvested mostly 30 Apr-29 May; BARI Mug 6 field duration 65 days. This leaves a Dec-Feb fallow gap after aman. In Amtali (Barguna) mungbean followed mustard (sown 23 Feb, harvested 6 May) before T. Aus.
water_implications: No irrigation in Polder 30 rabi crops; poor germination, lack of irrigation and pre-monsoon rain kept yields at 0.4-0.9 t/ha. In Khulna coastal saline soil frequent pond irrigation raised BINA Mung-2 germination by more than 20%.
soil_nutrient_implications: Legume: the IAEA coastal pilot lists mungbean among crops that fix nitrogen and improve soil quality for subsequent seasons. The N benefit is mainly realised by the next crop (see Mungbean to Rice).
pest_disease_break: BARI Mug 6 is listed as resistant to yellow mosaic virus. No rotation-specific pest/disease-break evidence found for rice to mungbean.
salinity_implications: BINA Mung-2 survived soil ECe 6.5-9.8 dS/m with irrigation water ECw 3.0-4.8 dS/m up to 45 days after sowing in Khulna coastal saline soil (topsoil salinity 3.8-13.8 dS/m Jan-May).
waterlogging_implications: Polder 30 mungbean and sesame were destroyed by waterlogging in 2012-13 after about 500 mm of cyclone rain in the last week of May; late-May rain is the key risk for a Feb-May mungbean crop.
system_yield_evidence: Khulna (Polder 30): Fallow-Rice-Mungbean rice-equivalent yield 8.8 t/ha/yr (aman-rabi range 6.6-10.0); aman-mungbean is a predominant existing Polder 30 system. Amtali: T. aman-mustard-mungbean-T. aus REY 14.16 t/ha.
region: Polder 30, Batiaghata, Khulna; Khulna coastal saline soil (SRDI/Khulna University)
source: Mondal et al. 2020 JISCAR 38(2); Saha et al. 2019 JISCAR 37(2); Bhuiyan et al. 2000 Khulna Univ. Studies; IAEA
notes: Mungbean here is a low-yield Feb-May crop; the value is mostly the nitrogen/soil benefit for the following T. Aman.

season_compatibility: Hybrid watermelon (Asian 2, 90 days) was sown 10 Dec-24 Jan in pits of 60x60x60 cm at 2x2 m in the LOW-salinity polders (Barisal division); it was not evaluated in Polder 30. Needs the same early T. Aman harvest and drainage as other rabi crops.
water_implications: Low-salinity sites irrigated rabi crops 2-4 times from canal water (0.1-0.6 dS/m). Mulched watermelon gave 42-63 t/ha vs 12-33 t/ha unmulched. Polder 30 had no reliable dry-season irrigation water after 2013, so feasibility there is unproven.
soil_nutrient_implications: Fertilizer was placed in the pits 5 days before sowing and N top-dressed three times; no soil-nutrient carry-over evidence found for rice to watermelon.
pest_disease_break: Cucurbits are susceptible hosts of Sclerotinia sclerotiorum; Fusarium wilt (F. oxysporum f. sp. niveum) builds up in continuously cropped watermelon soil. A flooded rice crop before watermelon is a break from cucurbit hosts and flooding suppresses some soil-borne fungi (shown for Verticillium in Japanese paddy-upland fields); a Fusarium-specific effect was not found.
salinity_implications: No watermelon salinity threshold sourced; the crop was tested only at low-salinity sites. Polder 30 topsoil salinity 2-16 dS/m; soil salinity is lowest Jul-Dec (monsoon and tidal water leach salts), intermediate Jan-Mar, and highest Apr-May (Polder 30 study). Rabi crops therefore meet rising salinity the later they are sown.
waterlogging_implications: Hybrid watermelon Asian 2 is listed as sensitive to waterlogging.
system_yield_evidence: Barisal low-salinity site: Rice-Rice-Watermelon rice-equivalent yield 21.7 t/ha/yr (highest of the rabi options tested). Not tested in Polder 30.
region: Polder 43/2F (Amtali, Barguna) and PSTU farm (Patuakhali) - low-salinity coastal sites
source: Mondal et al. 2020 JISCAR 38(2); PNW Handbook; Specialty Crop Grower; Springer (Verticillium paddy study)
notes: Use with caution for Polder 30 (medium salinity, no dry-season irrigation after 2013). Salinity threshold: no source found.

season_compatibility: Mustard sowing must be completed by the third week of November in southern Bangladesh; later sowing meets rising soil salinity and temperature. At Dacope (Khulna) T. Aman was harvested 22 Oct-20 Nov and BARI Sarisha-14 sown 25 Nov-3 Dec, harvested 20-27 Feb. A late aman harvest (up to 10 Dec in Polder 30 trials) closes the mustard window.
water_implications: Irrigation water with EC above 0.75 dS/m reduced winter-crop yields in the Dacope/Amtali trials; crops used residual moisture plus pond/canal irrigation where low-salinity water existed.
pest_disease_break: Brassica crops are hosts of Sclerotinia sclerotiorum; rotating with non-host cereals/grasses for at least 2 (best 3-8) years reduces sclerotia, and field flooding at warm temperatures destroys them (PNW Handbook). Rice is a non-host cereal, so T. Aman before mustard is a favourable break (general evidence).
salinity_implications: Delayed sowing cut mustard yield because soil salinity rose; soil and water salinity in the Dacope/Amtali trials rose from November and peaked in March/April. Polder 30 topsoil salinity 2-16 dS/m; soil salinity is lowest Jul-Dec (monsoon and tidal water leach salts), intermediate Jan-Mar, and highest Apr-May (Polder 30 study). Rabi crops therefore meet rising salinity the later they are sown.
waterlogging_implications: Late-drained aman fields (saturated about 15-45 days) push sowing past the third week of November; a mustard waterlogging tolerance value was not found.
system_yield_evidence: Dacope (Khulna): T. aman-Mustard-Fallow mustard 0.57 t/ha (0.77 and 0.36 in two years), system REY 6.00 t/ha vs 4.50 farmers' practice (+33.5%). Amtali: T. aman-Mustard-Mungbean-T. aus mustard 1.33 t/ha, REY 14.16 t/ha.
region: Dacope, Khulna and Amtali, Barguna (mustard not evaluated in Polder 30)
source: Saha et al. 2019 JISCAR 37(2); Springer mustard sowing-date study (southern Bangladesh); JISCAR wheat waterlogging paper; PNW Handbook
notes: Yields are low (0.36-1.61 t/ha). Soil-nutrient effect: no source found.

season_compatibility: Maize is sown mid-Dec to Jan (Dacope trials); T. Aman is transplanted from the first week of July to the first week of August in Polder 30 trials (about 10 Aug best for BRRI dhan52). No seasonal conflict found; the maize harvest date is not stated in the sources.
water_implications: T. Aman in Polder 30 is mostly rainfed with tidal water; no extra water constraint identified.
soil_nutrient_implications: Maize is a heavy nutrient drain (FAO ECOCROP). In Bangladesh T. Aman after maize, wheat or mungbean is usually grown with the previous residues removed, and the apparent N balance of T. Aman stayed negative (-9 to -53 kg N/ha/yr) in non-coastal trials, so N replacement for aman after maize matters.
salinity_implications: Wet-season T. Aman follows the monsoon leaching phase (soil salinity lowest Jul-Dec), so salinity carried over from the dry-season crop is reduced before aman. Polder 30 topsoil 2-16 dS/m.
waterlogging_implications: Polder monsoon water depths of 20-70 cm are normal for aman; submergence-tolerant varieties such as BRRI dhan52 are used.
region: Polder 30, Batiaghata, Khulna; non-coastal Bangladesh (Jashore) for N balance
source: Mondal et al. 2020 JISCAR 38(2); Akther et al. 2024 JISCAR 42(1); FAO ECOCROP; Jahan et al. 2019 Open Agriculture
notes: N balance figures come from Jashore/Bogra, not coastal sites. Pest/disease break: no source found.

season_compatibility: Sunflower sown mid-Nov (SRDI Batiaghata) with a 110-day field duration (Hysun 33) would be harvested about early March (derived from duration; harvest date not stated in the source), well before July aman transplanting.
water_implications: Aman is rainfed; sunflower's deep roots (2-3 m) draw on stored soil water during the dry season (FAO).
soil_nutrient_implications: No source found for sunflower residue or nutrient effects on the following T. Aman.
pest_disease_break: Sclerotinia sclerotia from a diseased sunflower crop persist 3-5 years in soil but are destroyed by field flooding at warm temperatures, so the flooded T. Aman crop is expected to draw inoculum down (general evidence applied as an inference); cereals such as rice are non-hosts.
salinity_implications: Polder 30 topsoil salinity 2-16 dS/m; soil salinity is lowest Jul-Dec (monsoon and tidal water leach salts), intermediate Jan-Mar, and highest Apr-May (Polder 30 study). Rabi crops therefore meet rising salinity the later they are sown.
waterlogging_implications: Aman is flood-tolerant (20-70 cm polder water depths normal); no conflict.
region: Polder 30, Batiaghata, Khulna
source: Mondal et al. 2020 JISCAR 38(2); Financial Express (SRDI Batiaghata); FAO Land & Water sunflower page; PNW Handbook
notes: Nutrient effect on aman: no source found.

season_compatibility: Polder 30 mungbean is harvested mostly 30 Apr-29 May and T. Aman is sown from the first week of July, leaving enough time. BARI trials chop and incorporate legume residue in situ one week before transplanting T. Aman.
soil_nutrient_implications: BARI Mung-2 took up 18.7-22.1 kg N/ha in seed and 29.0-30.2 kg N/ha in stover. Incorporating mungbean residue before T. Aman supplied about 7-18 kg N, 2-5 kg P and 8-17 kg K per ha and gave a slightly higher rice yield (about +0.02 to +0.04 t/ha, not statistically separated) with a less negative N balance. A residual legume N credit of 30-40 kg N/ha is commonly cited for the semi-arid tropics (general, not measured here).
salinity_implications: Mungbean tolerates soil ECe 6.5-9.8 dS/m for about 45 days in Khulna saline soil; the following monsoon phase leaches salts (soil salinity lowest Jul-Dec).
waterlogging_implications: Late-May cyclone rain destroyed Polder 30 mungbean in 2013; the flooded aman phase follows.
system_yield_evidence: Khulna (Polder 30): Fallow-Rice-Mungbean REY 8.8 t/ha/yr. Amtali: T. aman-Mustard-Mungbean-T. aus REY 14.16 t/ha.
region: Jashore (AEZ-11), Mymensingh and Jamalpur for N effect; Polder 30 for timing
source: Sarker et al. 2011 BJAR 36(2); Jahan et al. 2019 Open Agriculture; Mondal et al. 2020 JISCAR 38(2); Bhuiyan et al. 2000 Khulna Univ. Studies; IAEA
notes: N-effect numbers are from non-coastal Bangladesh trials. Pest/disease break: no source found.

season_compatibility: Watermelon (90 days, sown 10 Dec-24 Jan at low-salinity sites) finishes well before July aman; not tested in Polder 30.
pest_disease_break: Rotating out of watermelon lowers Fusarium wilt build-up: fusarium wilt levels fell 20%, 40% and 50% after one, two and three years of fallow, and a green-garlic rotation improved yield and reduced disease in continuously cropped watermelon. Paddy flooding reduced Verticillium propagules in Japanese paddy-upland fields; a Fusarium-specific effect of flooded rice was not found.
salinity_implications: Polder 30 topsoil salinity 2-16 dS/m; soil salinity is lowest Jul-Dec (monsoon and tidal water leach salts), intermediate Jan-Mar, and highest Apr-May (Polder 30 study). Rabi crops therefore meet rising salinity the later they are sown.
waterlogging_implications: Aman is flood-tolerant; watermelon itself is waterlogging-sensitive so it must be off the field before flooding.
system_yield_evidence: Barisal low-salinity site: Rice-Rice-Watermelon REY 21.7 t/ha/yr. Not tested in Polder 30.
region: Barisal division low-salinity polders; China and Japan studies for disease evidence
source: Mondal et al. 2020 JISCAR 38(2); Specialty Crop Grower; PLOS ONE 2016 (Yang et al.); Springer (Verticillium paddy study)
notes: Disease evidence is from outside Bangladesh.

season_compatibility: Mustard (BARI Sarisha-14) sown 25 Nov-3 Dec was harvested 20-27 Feb at Dacope, leaving a long fallow before aman (transplanted 8-10 Aug there); in Amtali mungbean and T. Aus filled the gap (mustard harvest 19 Feb, mungbean sown 23 Feb).
pest_disease_break: Brassica crops host Sclerotinia sclerotiorum; the flooded T. Aman crop that follows is a non-host cereal phase and flooding at warm temperatures destroys sclerotia (PNW Handbook, general evidence applied as an inference).
salinity_implications: Polder 30 topsoil salinity 2-16 dS/m; soil salinity is lowest Jul-Dec (monsoon and tidal water leach salts), intermediate Jan-Mar, and highest Apr-May (Polder 30 study). Rabi crops therefore meet rising salinity the later they are sown.
system_yield_evidence: Dacope: T. aman-Mustard-Fallow system REY 6.00 t/ha vs 4.50 farmers' practice. Amtali: T. aman-Mustard-Mungbean-T. aus REY 14.16 t/ha.
region: Dacope, Khulna and Amtali, Barguna
source: Saha et al. 2019 JISCAR 37(2); PNW Handbook
notes: Soil-nutrient effect: no source found.

season_compatibility: Farmers' baseline is Fallow-Fallow-T. Aman (cropping intensity about 100-114%). Aman-Boro was evaluated in Polder 30 in 2005-2007: Boro sown 7-15 November gave the best and most consistent yield (about 5.0 t/ha); late-October sowing was damaged by cold at panicle initiation.
water_implications: Boro needs pumped irrigation from polder canals; canal water stayed below 4 dS/m until April when the sluice was managed (2006, 2007, 2012), but from 2013 the partly open sluice made the canal water unsuitable, so irrigated Boro was no longer supported.
soil_nutrient_implications: T. Aman apparent N balance stayed negative (-9 to -53 kg N/ha/yr) even with fertilizer in non-coastal Bangladesh trials; rice depletes N without a legume in the sequence.
salinity_implications: Boro yield in medium-saline Polder 30 ranged from almost zero to 6.3 t/ha vs 4.4-7.9 t/ha in low-salinity sites, attributed to salinity plus cold at panicle initiation. Polder 30 topsoil salinity 2-16 dS/m; soil salinity is lowest Jul-Dec (monsoon and tidal water leach salts), intermediate Jan-Mar, and highest Apr-May (Polder 30 study). Rabi crops therefore meet rising salinity the later they are sown.
waterlogging_implications: Polder land often remains flooded or saturated until December, delaying aman harvest and any following crop.
system_yield_evidence: Khulna (Polder 30): Fallow-Rice-Rice (aman-boro) REY 8.0 t/ha/yr (range 4.7-10.5; 8.8-10.2 with Boro sown 7-15 Nov) vs farmers' 2-3 t/ha aman plus 0-1 t/ha rabi.
region: Polder 30, Batiaghata, Khulna
source: Mondal et al. 2020 JISCAR 38(2); Jahan et al. 2019 Open Agriculture
notes: Monoculture pest/disease build-up for rice: no source found.
